items.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 25, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: So Monk Rowe is one of my new guys I like, he’s got a little website, I can order his records...

ctx.x: The fighter. And even Keter Betts and Houston [Person] were talking about, “Man when he would fight, everyone, it was like that was a rallying point. It was like well they could kick us down but we’ve got the best athletes and we’ve got the best artists. And so we saw, when I was a kid, Leotyne Price, and we were so proud. It was like when we walked © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

into the hall, my mother and father’s head just went a little bit higher. Because they were saying she’s ours. This is something that we’re proud of. And you can oppress us in all these other kinds of ways. But we’ve got these great artists, like Lena Horne they were so proud of, and they took me to see her. items.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 25, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I’m very pleased to re-connect with Byron Stripling, who did a memorable series of shows for me 22 years ago.

ctx.x: Byron was interviewed via Zoom on June 25, 2020, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

My name is Monk Rowe for the Fillius Jazz Archive at Hamilton College, and I’m very pleased to re-connect with Byron Stripling, who did a memorable series of shows for me 22 years ago. I think we both look exactly the same.
